skill.name: building-agent-tools

skill.summary: Build clear, efficient tool interfaces that help AI agents complete workflows reliably.

content.user_title: Design Effective Tools for AI Agents
content.value_statement: Poor tool interfaces waste tokens and force agents through fragile workflows. This guide helps teams design consolidated, namespaced tools with clear schemas, efficient responses, and actionable errors.
actual_capabilities: Define an agent tool's purpose and identify consolidation opportunities.
Design descriptive, namespaced tool names and clear parameters.
Shape high-signal responses with semantic identifiers and selectable detail.
Apply pagination, filtering, defaults, and intelligent truncation.
Validate tools using agent workflows, token consumption, and recoverable errors.
Structure MCP schemas with explicit required and optional parameters.
limitations: Provides design guidance, not runnable implementations or generated source code.
Does not test tools or measure token usage automatically.
Does not define authentication, authorization, rate limiting, or deployment controls.
Covers MCP patterns at a high level without protocol-specific examples.

use_cases.title: Design Agent APIs
use_cases.description: Plan consolidated API operations with clear parameters, meaningful responses, and predictable recovery paths.

use_cases.title: Structure MCP Tools
use_cases.description: Create namespaced MCP tool families with descriptive schemas and explicit required fields.

use_cases.title: Improve Tool Catalogs
use_cases.description: Review existing tools for redundant calls, excessive output, vague descriptions, and unusable identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a New Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed agent tool: [description]. Define its purpose, users, core operation, parameters, and expected response. Keep the design concise.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a simple agent tool design

prompt_templates.title: Review a Tool Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this tool interface: [interface details]. Identify unclear names, missing constraints, weak defaults, raw identifiers, and response fields that waste tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate a Tool Family
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related tools: [tool list]. Propose a smaller namespaced set that supports common workflows with fewer calls and clear operation boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign [interface and workflow] for agent reliability. Include pagination, filtering, response detail options, semantic identifiers, actionable errors, and a realistic validation plan.

output_examples.input: Design a calendar scheduling tool for an agent.
output: Recommendation: use one scheduling operation that checks availability and creates the event.
Inputs: attendees, time range, duration, time zone, and optional location.
Response: confirmed time, attendee status, readable calendar names, and recovery guidance.

output_examples.input: Review separate project search, task search, and user search tools.
output: Keep clear service namespacing across the tool family.
Consolidate only operations that share a common agent workflow.
Add filters, pagination defaults, readable identifiers, and concise or detailed response options.

best_practices: Test designs with complete agent workflows, including errors and follow-up actions.
Return enough context for the next decision while limiting unnecessary fields.
Use consistent names, parameter constraints, defaults, and response conventions across each tool family.
anti_patterns: Do not create many single-purpose tools when one coherent operation supports the common workflow.
Do not return raw identifiers or large unfiltered datasets without useful context.
Do not use vague descriptions or errors that leave the agent without a recovery path.

faq.question: Does this skill generate MCP server code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design principles and review guidance for tool interfaces and responses.

faq.question: Can I use it for non-MCP APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The naming, consolidation, response, pagination, and error guidance applies to most agent-facing APIs.

faq.question: How does it reduce token usage?
faq.answer: It recommends filtering, pagination, intelligent truncation, structured responses, and selectable response detail.

faq.question: Does it cover tool security?
faq.answer: No. Add separate reviews for authentication, authorization, input validation, data exposure, and operational controls.

faq.question: Should every related operation become one tool?
faq.answer: No. Consolidate operations that support one common workflow while preserving clear and predictable boundaries.

faq.question: How should I validate a design?
faq.answer: Test realistic agent workflows, measure response size, inspect errors, and confirm that outputs support the next action.
